calc.title: Storage rent calculator
calc.feeHint: The most a miner can take each time the box becomes “overdue”.
calc.minHint: A box below this value can't be created in the first place.
calc.tooShort: Less than 1 period — a miner can take the whole box once it's overdue.
calc.lives: {{periods}} periods ≈ {{years}} years if it's never touched

intro: Every Ergo node has to keep the entire set of unspent boxes (the UTXO set) to validate new transactions. That set can only grow: people create new boxes all the time, while forgotten boxes — wallets with lost seeds, token dust, developer experiments — sit there forever. In Bitcoin, users pay a fee once when creating an output, and then get stored for free, forever, on every node's machine. Ergo answers the question “who pays for storage forever?” with storage rent (also called demurrage).

rule.title: The rule
rule.p1: If a box sits untouched — not spent, not “refreshed” — for {{period}} blocks (≈ {{years}} years), a miner is allowed to touch it even without the key:
rule.li1: If the box's value is greater than the fee: the miner takes exactly the fee, and must recreate an identical box (same script, tokens and registers) holding the value minus the fee, with a new creation height. The 4-year clock starts again.
rule.li2: If the box's value is less than the fee: the miner takes everything in it — the ERG and any tokens or NFTs — and the box disappears from the UTXO set.
rule.p2: The fee is based on the box's size:
rule.code:
fee = boxSizeInBytes × storageFeeFactor
storageFeeFactor = {{factor}} nanoERG / byte  (= {{factorErg}} ERG / byte, default value)

warn.title: Tokens and NFTs are not exempt
warn.text: Rent is paid in ERG, but when a box can no longer cover it the miner claims the whole box, tokens included. A box that holds a valuable NFT next to the bare-minimum ERG is exactly the kind that gets emptied first if it is left untouched for years.

params.title: Votable parameters
params.text: storageFeeFactor and minValuePerByte are network parameters. Miners vote to change them through the votes field in the header, so the actual values may differ from the defaults above. The 4-year period itself is different: changing it would take a hard fork, which the community generally avoids.

example.title: A worked example
example.p1: A typical wallet box (P2PK, no tokens) is around 100 bytes. The fee per period is 100 × {{factor}} = {{fee}} nanoERG = {{feeErg}} ERG every 4 years. For a box holding 10 ERG, that's 1.25% every 4 years — and it only applies if you don't touch your wallet for the full 4 years. Sending your funds to yourself once resets the clock.
example.p2: Ergo's own explainer puts the typical charge at about 0.14 ERG plus a transaction fee per box — slightly more than our 100-byte figure, because real wallet boxes are often a little bigger. The same explainer notes that a box holding 1 ERG would take about 32 years of total inactivity before a miner could empty it — for a 100-byte box that is exactly 8 periods × 0.125 ERG. The calculator below starts from exactly that case.

min.title: Minimum box value
min.p1: The flip side of storage rent is the minimum value rule: every box must hold at least {{min}} nanoERG × size (by default). This stops anyone from creating millions of “dust” boxes almost for free to bloat the UTXO set. It's why the minimum output in a wallet is usually around 0.001 ERG — comfortably above the minimum even for larger boxes carrying tokens.

good.title: Why this is a good thing
good.bloat: Prevents state bloat: abandoned data is gradually cleared out of the UTXO set, so the cost of running a node doesn't grow forever.
good.dust: Garbage collection for dust: tiny amounts scattered across thousands of forgotten boxes are the first to be swept up, because they can't cover even one period of rent.
good.income: Steady income for miners: once emission ends, storage rent is a revenue stream that doesn't depend on how busy the network is — on top of transaction fees and EIP-27 re-emission.
good.lost: Lost coins return to circulation: ERG in a wallet with a lost seed isn't locked away forever as it would be with Bitcoin; it slowly flows back to miners. That keeps coins in circulation and softens the slow deflation every capped-supply coin suffers from lost keys.
good.fair: Fairness: those who take up more storage (bigger boxes) pay more than those who take up less.

real.title: It has already happened
real.text: Ergo mainnet launched in July 2019, so the very first boxes reached the {{period}}-block mark around mid-2023 — since then, storage rent has been a real part of mainnet economics rather than a theory.

avoid.title: How do I avoid paying it?
avoid.p1: Simple: every so often (less than once every 4 years), spend your boxes — for example, send your whole balance to yourself. New boxes are created with a new height, and the clock starts over.
avoid.p2: Rent is charged per box, so it also helps to consolidate: sending everything to one of your addresses in a single transaction merges many small boxes into a few larger ones — fewer boxes that could ever be charged, and each one far from the danger zone.
avoid.p3: Want to understand where a box's size comes from? See <box>Boxes & registers</box>.
